question: 一件事被解释清楚，就变得不值钱了吗？
question_en: Does explaining something drain the value out of it?
sub: 知道彩虹是折射的人照样看彩虹；可一听爱是催产素，很多人当场觉得被贬低了。
sub_en: Nobody stops looking at rainbows once they learn about refraction — yet tell someone their love is oxytocin and they feel demoted on the spot.

casting.reason: 「花的美不会因为我知道它的结构而减少，只会增加」——这句话是当着一位说科学家把花拆成零件的画家朋友讲的。他在这道题上的立场因此非常干脆：知识只做加法，觉得掉价的人多半是把『不懂』误当成了『神秘』。他也咬住另一头——最容易骗到的人是自己，所以一个说不出什么情况下算错的『解释』，本来就不配让人为它掉价。
casting.reason_en: “The beauty of a flower is not lessened by my knowing its structure — it is added to.” He said that to a painter friend who accused scientists of taking a flower apart. His position here is correspondingly blunt: knowledge only ever adds, and whoever feels devalued has mistaken not-understanding for mystery. He holds the other end just as firmly — the easiest person to fool is yourself, so an “explanation” that cannot say what would prove it wrong never deserved anyone's awe in the first place.

casting.reason: 五十岁上，《战争与和平》早已写完，名利俱全，他却开始把绳子藏起来，怕自己夜里上吊。《忏悔录》记下的正是这道题最硬的那一半：科学把一切都告诉了他，唯独不回答『我为什么活着、死后还剩下什么』。于是他要在解释与回答之间划一条线，并坚持这条线不能靠追加更多的解释抹掉。
casting.reason_en: At fifty, with War and Peace long finished and fame and fortune secured, he began hiding the rope, afraid of hanging himself in the night. A Confession records the hardest half of this question: science had told him everything except why he was alive and what would remain of him. So he draws a line between explaining and answering, and insists that no amount of further explanation can rub that line out.

casting.reason: 《人间词话》立境界说，最重一个『隔』字：语语都在目前是不隔，一著理语议论便隔。这道题到他手上因此变成位置之争——不是不许解说，而是解说一旦横在人与物之间，再见此花，先起于心的已是注脚。
casting.reason_en: Renjian Cihua builds its poetics on jingjie, and turns on a single word: ge, the veil. When every line stands immediately before the eye there is no veil; the moment argument and abstraction enter, the veil falls. In his hands the question becomes one of placement — not whether explanation is permitted, but that once it stands between a person and a thing, what rises first at the next sight of the flower is the footnote.

casting.reason: 心里那个想努力就努力的『自主人』，在他看来是我们解释不了行为时请来顶账的影子；解释掉它是进步，不是损失。他给出这一桌最不留情的立场：掉价感属于那个被夺走功劳的幻影，不属于你，而每解释掉一段行为，能动手改的东西就多一点。
casting.reason_en: The “autonomous man” inside — the little agent who tries hard because he chooses to — is, on his account, a stand-in we hire whenever behaviour outruns our explanations; explaining him away is progress, not loss. His is the least consoling position at the table: the sense of being cheapened belongs to that phantom, who is losing credit he never earned, and not to you — and every stretch of behaviour explained is one more thing you can actually change.

casting.reason: 用 fMRI 扫过热恋中的大脑之后，她主张浪漫爱不是情绪而是一套驱力，并把爱拆成性欲、吸引、依恋三套可以各走各的系统。被问得最多的正是这道题：知道了这些，还怎么相信爱情。她的答案是拆解不取消——恰恰在失恋和热恋退潮的那一刻，机制给得出别的话给不出的具体办法。
casting.reason_en: After putting people in the throes of love into an fMRI scanner, she argued that romantic love is not an emotion but a drive, and took love apart into three systems — sex, attraction and attachment — that can run independently of one another. The question she is asked most often is precisely this one: knowing all that, how can you still believe in love? Her answer is that taking something apart does not cancel it — and that at the moment of a breakup, or when the first rush fades, the mechanism yields practical help nothing else does.

casting.reason: 一切主张到他这里都先挨一问：你说的那样东西，有没有不依赖他缘而自己成立的自性？掉价感于是被重新描述——众人以为价值藏在物中，说明一到便被取走；他要指出那个仓库从来是空的，而世俗谛里的彩虹依旧宛然可爱。二谛不相碍，两头都不必丢。
casting.reason_en: Every claim that reaches him meets one question first: does the thing you name possess any nature of its own, standing free of every condition? The feeling of devaluation is then redescribed — people take value to be stored inside the thing, and explanation to have emptied the store; he means to show the store was always empty, while the rainbow of conventional truth remains as lovely as ever. The two truths do not obstruct one another, and neither end need be surrendered.

casting.reason: 这道题在他的实验室里是可测的：糖片止痛调动内源性阿片，纳洛酮挡得掉；而把同一剂镇痛药偷偷输进病人体内、不让他知道时间，效力立刻掉一大截。他带来的结论与直觉相反——说破不必然让效力消失，藏起来才会。医生的语气与诊室的仪式，在他那里不是包装，是有生理作用的成分。
casting.reason_en: In his laboratory this question is measurable: a sugar pill recruits endogenous opioids and naloxone can block the effect, while the same dose of a painkiller infused without the patient knowing when it arrives loses a large share of its power. His finding cuts against intuition — saying it out loud does not necessarily destroy the effect, concealment does. A doctor's tone and the ritual of the consulting room are not packaging to him; they are active ingredients with physiological effects.

casting.reason: 济慈的指控点名的是他：拆开白光，就等于把彩虹的诗意解散了。可他一生写神学与年代学的字数多过力学，从没觉得算准了轨道天空会变小。他要把这项指控翻译成一个技术问题——你说被拿走的那样东西，具体是哪一条？
casting.reason_en: Keats's charge names him: split white light and you have dissolved the poetry of the rainbow. Yet he wrote more on theology and chronology than on mechanics, and never felt the sky shrink because an orbit had been computed. He wants the accusation restated as a technical question — the thing you say was taken away, which item was it exactly?

posts.text: 说我拆散了彩虹的人，请把账目算清楚：棱镜之后，虹仍挂在天上，颜色一样不少，多出来的是它为何总在雨后、总在背着太阳的那一侧。**算得越准，那位设计者的手艺越显出来，而不是越少。**我一生写神学与年代学的字数多过力学，从没觉得天空因此变小。至于失落——觉得被拿走了什么的人，往往说不出被拿走的是哪一条。那不是损失，是不习惯。
posts.text_en: Whoever says I pulled the rainbow apart should first settle the accounts. After the prism, the bow still hangs in the sky, not one colour short, and what has been added is why it always comes after rain and always on the side away from the sun. **The more exactly it is computed, the more the craftsmanship of its designer shows — not the less.** I wrote more pages on theology and chronology than on mechanics, and never once felt the sky grow smaller for it. As for the sense of loss: those who feel something was taken from them can rarely name which item it was. That is not loss. That is unfamiliarity.

posts.text: 账算得再清楚，也没有回答我五十岁那年夜里问自己的话：我为什么活着，我死后还剩下什么。科学能告诉我地球绕日、细胞分裂、我的悲伤是某种化学；对『我该怎么活』它一个字也答不上。**掉价的从来不是那件事本身，是我原先靠它撑住的那个意义。**我不反对解释，我反对拿解释冒充回答——那是一次偷换，而且偷走的正是人最后攥着的那点东西。
posts.text_en: However exactly the accounts are settled, they do not answer what I asked myself in the night of my fiftieth year: why am I alive, and what remains of me once I am dead. Science can tell me the earth goes round the sun, that cells divide, that my grief is a certain chemistry. To the question of how I ought to live it says nothing at all. **What loses its value is never the thing explained; it is the meaning I had been propping up with it.** I do not object to explanation. I object to explanation passing itself off as an answer — a substitution that takes from a man the last thing he was holding.

posts.text: 这一刀砍错了地方。我有位画家朋友说，他看得见花的美，而我这个科学家把花拆成了一堆枯燥的零件。我的回答是：细胞里的结构、蜜蜂看得见而我们看不见的颜色、花与虫几亿年互相塑造出的样子——**这些只往那朵花上添东西，知识做的是加法，它从不减去你原来看见的那一层。**至于人生的意义，它本来就不在我这张桌子上，我没拿走过，也不打算替谁保管。
posts.text_en: That blade has landed in the wrong place. I have a painter friend who says he can see the beauty of a flower, while I as a scientist take it apart into a heap of dull components. My answer is this: the structure inside the cells, the colours a bee can see and we cannot, the shape that flowers and insects have worked into each other over hundreds of millions of years — **all of it is added to that flower. Knowledge only ever adds; it never subtracts the layer you were already seeing.** As for the meaning of life, that was never on my table. I did not take it, and I am not offering to hold it for anyone.

posts.text: 诸君只论加减，未及一『隔』字。词以境界为最上；其言情也沁人心脾，其写景也豁人耳目，读之如亲历。一下注脚，则物与我之间横一层解说：**语语都在目前者为不隔，著理语议论者即隔。**费曼谓知识只添不减——添于所知则然，添于目前之境则未必。牛顿之虹，算之愈精而愈明；李后主之愁，释为多巴胺，则愁已不在纸上矣。
posts.text_en: You are all keeping accounts of what is added and subtracted, and none of you has touched the word ge — the veil. In poetry jingjie stands highest: feeling so rendered that it soaks into the reader, scene so rendered that the eye is opened, until to read is to have been there. Let a footnote down, and a layer of exposition lies between the thing and me. **Where every line stands immediately before the eye there is no veil; where argument and abstraction enter, the veil has fallen.** Feynman says knowledge only adds. To what is known, yes; to what stands before the eye, not necessarily. Newton's rainbow grows brighter the more exactly it is reckoned. Li Yu's sorrow, rendered as dopamine, is no longer on the page.
posts.vernacular: 诸位只在算加减，谁也没碰到一个『隔』字。词以境界为最高；写情要能沁人心脾，写景要能让人耳目一新，读起来就像自己亲身到过。可一旦加上注脚，事物与我之间就横了一层解说：**句句都直接呈现在眼前的叫不隔，一讲道理、一发议论就隔了。**费曼说知识只添不减——添在知识上确实如此，添在眼前这一境上就未必。牛顿的彩虹，算得越精越清楚；李后主的愁，一旦解释成多巴胺，那份愁就不在纸上了。

glossary.境界: jingjie（境界）：王国维《人间词话》评词的最高标准，指一首作品所开出的那个完整的情景世界——写情能沁人心脾，写景能豁人耳目，读者如同亲历。

glossary_en.jingjie: The highest criterion in Wang Guowei's poetics: the whole world of scene and feeling that a work opens up — feeling rendered so that it soaks into the reader, scene rendered so that the eye is opened, until reading is a kind of having been there.

posts.text: 那层注脚正是我要的东西。人心里那个『自主人』——想看花就看花、想努力就努力的小人儿——是我们解释不了行为时请来顶账的。每解释掉一段行为，他就缩小一点；**他缩得越小，你能动手改的东西就越多。**说被贬低了：被贬低的不是你，是那个从来没干过活、却年年领功劳的影子。戒不掉烟的人需要的不是对意志的敬意，是一间被重新摆过的屋子。
posts.text_en: That layer of footnote is exactly what I am after. The autonomous man inside — the little agent who looks at the flower because he chooses to and works hard because he wills it — is a stand-in we hire whenever behaviour outruns our explanations. Every stretch of behaviour explained shrinks him a little. **The smaller he gets, the more there is that you can actually change.** You say you feel cheapened. What is being cheapened is not you; it is a shadow that has never done a day's work and collects the credit every year. A man who cannot stop smoking does not need respect paid to his willpower. He needs a room rearranged.

glossary.自主人: autonomous man（自主人）：斯金纳用来指人们设想在行为背后自行做主的那个内在行动者；他认为这是行为尚未被解释清楚时请来顶账的虚构人物。

glossary_en.autonomous man: Skinner's name for the inner agent people posit behind behaviour, choosing and willing on its own; in his view a fiction hired to cover whatever behaviour has not yet been explained.

posts.text: 我扫过正在热恋的人的脑子：看爱人的照片时，亮起来的是腹侧被盖区——和渴求同一套回路，不是情绪区。所以我说浪漫爱是一种驱力，像饿，像渴。有人听完说：那我的爱情不过是化学。可我从没见过谁因为知道饥饿是血糖调节就不吃饭。**被减掉的不是爱，是你以为爱必须毫无来由的那份天真。**知道它是驱力，才解释得了为什么被甩的人会像戒断一样发抖。
posts.text_en: I have scanned the brains of people in the first throes of love. Looking at a photograph of the beloved lights up the ventral tegmental area — the same circuitry as craving, not the emotion centres. That is why I call romantic love a drive, like hunger, like thirst. People hear this and say: so my love is only chemistry. Yet I have never met anyone who stopped eating on learning that hunger is blood-sugar regulation. **What gets subtracted is not the love. It is your assumption that love has to come from nowhere.** Knowing it is a drive is what explains why someone who has just been left shakes like a person in withdrawal.

posts.text: 诸法从缘起，我说即是空。空者非谓无有，谓无自性耳。今诸君所争，同一执也：以为物中先藏一『值钱』之自性，说明既至，此性遂被取去。然则未说明时，此性又安在？**若价值实有自性，则说与不说皆不能增减；既随说明而减，可知其从来不在物中，而在缘中。**依二谛观之：世俗谛中彩虹宛然可爱，胜义谛中彩虹无自性，两不相碍。
posts.text_en: All things arise from conditions; this I call emptiness. Emptiness does not mean non-existence — it means the absence of a nature of one's own. What you are all disputing rests on a single grip: you take a thing to hold some inherent worth in store, which explanation then comes and removes. But before the explanation arrived, where was that worth kept? **If value had a nature of its own, no telling or withholding could add to it or take from it; and since it shrinks when something is explained, it was never in the thing at all, but in the conditions.** Seen by the two truths: in conventional truth the rainbow is lovely just as it appears, in ultimate truth it has no nature of its own, and neither obstructs the other.
posts.vernacular: 一切事物都由条件聚合而生，我把这叫作空。空不是说什么都没有，是说没有独立自存的自性。你们现在争的其实是同一个执着：以为事物里面先存着一份『值钱』的自性，解释一到就被拿走了。可在没解释之前，那份自性又放在哪里？**如果价值真有自性，那么说不说都不能增减它；既然一被解释就减少，可见它从来就不在事物里面，而在条件之中。**按二谛来看：在世俗谛里，彩虹依然清清楚楚地可爱；在胜义谛里，彩虹并无自性——两者互不妨碍。

glossary.二谛: two truths（二谛）：中观区分世俗谛与胜义谛——前者是日常约定中成立的真实（彩虹可爱、钱能买米），后者是就自性而言的究竟审察（一切法无自性）；二者不相违。

glossary_en.two truths: The Madhyamaka distinction between conventional truth — what holds within everyday usage, that a rainbow is lovely and money buys rice — and ultimate truth, the analysis that finds no independent nature in anything. The two do not contradict each other.

posts.text: 我在实验室里干的正是『说破』这件事。糖片止痛是真的，它调动内源性阿片，用纳洛酮就能挡掉——这套机制我们拆得很细。按诸位的忧虑，拆完它该失效了。可开放标签安慰剂告诉我们：明确告知病人『这是不含药物成分的安慰剂』，肠易激、慢性腰痛、疲劳照样好转。**被解释掉的是骗术，不是效力。**医生的语气、诊室的仪式，不是包装，是有生理作用的成分。
posts.text_en: Saying it out loud is precisely what I do for a living. The analgesia from a sugar pill is real: it recruits endogenous opioids, and naloxone can block it — we have taken the mechanism apart in fine detail. On the worry expressed around this table, it should have stopped working once we did. Yet open-label placebo tells us otherwise: tell patients plainly that what they are taking is a placebo with no active drug in it, and irritable bowel, chronic back pain and fatigue still improve. **What gets explained away is the deception, not the efficacy.** A doctor's tone and the ritual of the consulting room are not packaging. They are ingredients with physiological effects.

glossary.开放标签安慰剂: open-label placebo（开放标签安慰剂）：在明确告知受试者所服为不含药物成分的安慰剂之后，仍然给予的安慰剂治疗；多项试验中它对疼痛、肠易激等症状仍有可测的改善。

glossary_en.open-label placebo: A placebo given after the patient has been told outright that it contains no active drug; in a number of trials it still produces measurable improvement in pain, irritable bowel syndrome and related complaints.

posts.text: 斯金纳欲以重排屋子了此一事，然则重排者谁？**吾所惜者非影子之功名，乃目前之一境**：见花而心先动，此动不待解说而后有。君之术能令人不吸烟，不能令人见花而喜。世谓此为祛魅——魅去而术存，术存而味失。且解说之害不在其伪，在其先入：注脚读熟，则再见此花，先起者已是注脚，非花矣。此所以知之愈多而味之愈薄也。
posts.text_en: Skinner would settle the whole matter by rearranging the room — but who is doing the rearranging? **What I grieve for is not a shadow's credit; it is the moment as it stands before the eye**: the heart stirs at the sight of a flower, and that stirring does not wait upon explanation. Your art can stop a man smoking. It cannot make him glad at the sight of a flower. The age calls this disenchantment — the magic goes, the technique remains, and with the technique comes the loss of savour. And the harm of exposition lies not in its being false but in its coming first: once the footnote is known by heart, what rises at the next sight of the flower is the footnote, not the flower. This is how it comes about that the more one knows, the thinner the taste.
posts.vernacular: 斯金纳想靠重新摆一间屋子把这件事解决掉，可重新摆屋子的又是谁？**我可惜的不是那个影子的功劳，而是眼前的这一境**：看见花，心先动了一下，这一动并不等解释来了才有。你的办法能让人戒烟，却不能让人看见花就欢喜。世人把这个过程叫祛魅——魅力没了，技术还在；技术还在，味道却没了。而且解说之害不在它说错，在它抢先：注脚读熟之后，再见到这朵花，最先浮上来的已经是注脚，不是花了。知道得越多，味道越薄，就是这么来的。

glossary.祛魅: disenchantment（祛魅）：韦伯用来描述现代化进程的用语——原则上一切都可以通过计算与技术掌握，世界不再有神秘莫测的力量，意义因此退出公共解释。

glossary_en.disenchantment: Weber's term for the modern condition in which everything is in principle masterable by calculation and technique, no incalculable forces remain, and meaning withdraws from public explanation.

posts.text: 注脚读熟便再也见不到花——这是个可以测的说法，而我们测过它的反面。告诉病人手里这片是安慰剂，效果没有被抹掉；真正抹掉效果的是另一件事：隐藏给药。同一剂镇痛药，护士当面注射，和由电脑在病人不知情时输入，**后者的效力立刻掉一大截——藏起来比说破更伤效果。**注脚不必与花争位置；怕的是根本没有人对你说话。
posts.text_en: Once the footnote is known by heart the flower can never be seen again — that is a testable claim, and we have tested its opposite. Tell a patient the tablet in their hand is a placebo and the effect is not wiped out. What does wipe it out is something else: hidden administration. Give the same dose of painkiller by a nurse at the bedside, or by a computer at a moment the patient knows nothing about, and **the concealed dose loses a large part of its power. Hiding costs more than telling.** The footnote need not compete with the flower for space. What you should fear is nobody speaking to you at all.

glossary.隐藏给药: hidden administration（隐藏给药）：由预设程序在病人不知情的时刻输入药物，以剥离期待与治疗仪式的作用；同一剂量下其疗效显著低于当面给药，差额即心理社会情境的贡献。

glossary_en.hidden administration: Delivering a drug by a preprogrammed pump at a moment the patient is unaware of, so as to strip out expectation and the ritual of treatment; at the same dose it works markedly less well than an open injection, and the difference measures what the psychosocial context contributes.

posts.text: 『我为什么活着』这个问句本身就是坏问题：它先假定行为背后有个不依赖后果的理由，再因为找不到而痛苦。那一年救了托尔斯泰的不是答案，是他开始干活——下地、办学、教农民的孩子识字，行为被结果强化，人就稳住了。**先要意义再行动的人，两样多半都拿不到；先行动的人，意义是行动的副产品。**你们把这叫贬低，我叫它可操作。
posts.text_en: Why am I alive is a badly formed question to begin with: it presupposes a reason behind behaviour that owes nothing to consequences, and then makes a man miserable for failing to find one. What saved Tolstoy that year was not an answer but the fact that he started working — the fields, the school, teaching peasant children their letters. Behaviour was reinforced by its consequences and the man steadied. **Those who demand meaning before acting usually get neither; for those who act, meaning is a by-product.** You call this a demotion. I call it something you can do.

posts.text: 价值不在物中而在缘中——这一条我不接受。**引力不因谁看见、谁命名而增减一分；同一条平方反比律，在苹果上与在月球上一样成立。**它在那里，与约定无关。至于诸位担心的贬低：我算出潮汐由日月牵引之后，海并没有变浅。人心里那点失落我承认存在，但那是人的失落，不是世界的损失——把它记到自然的账上，是记错了本。
posts.text_en: That value lies not in the thing but in its conditions — this I do not accept. **Gravitation neither grows nor shrinks according to who observes or names it; one and the same inverse-square law holds for the apple and for the moon.** It is there, and no convention put it there. As for the devaluation that worries this table: after I worked out that the tides are drawn by the sun and moon, the sea did not become shallower. I grant that the sense of loss exists, but it is a loss on the human side, not a loss to the world — and to enter it in nature's ledger is to enter it in the wrong book.

posts.text: 怕注脚横在人与物之间的，不妨来看看真人。我把那三套系统讲给一屋子人听：性欲、浪漫吸引、依恋，它们可以各走各的——所以你会对配偶有深厚的依恋，同时被另一个人吸引。**听懂的人多数不是从此不爱了，而是终于不再把一阵冲动当成必须拆掉全家的天意。**王国维要的『先受』我不反对；我只是发现，解释给了人一只还能扶住方向盘的手。
posts.text_en: Anyone afraid that the footnote will come between a person and the world should look at actual people. I explain the three systems to a roomful of them: sex drive, romantic attraction and attachment can each run on their own track — which is how you can hold a deep attachment to a spouse and feel pulled towards someone else at the same time. **Most of those who take that in do not stop loving. They stop mistaking a surge of feeling for a decree that the household must be dismantled.** I have nothing against Wang Guowei's insistence on undergoing a thing first. I have only found that an explanation leaves a person one hand still on the wheel.

glossary.依恋: attachment（依恋）：费舍尔所划三套脑系统之一，以催产素与血管加压素为主，表现为长期的安稳联结与分离焦虑，与激烈短暂的浪漫吸引分属不同回路。

glossary_en.attachment: One of the three brain systems Fisher distinguishes, running largely on oxytocin and vasopressin: the calm, durable bond, along with the anxiety of separation — a different circuit from the intense and short-lived system of romantic attraction.

posts.text: 以引力为不待人而立，此正吾所破之自性见。吾未尝言律不成、海变浅；吾言：律成于所量之物、所用之尺、所立之系，离此三者，『引力』一名何所指？**汝能指出一物，不待他缘而独自成其为重者乎？**不能，则律非无，特非自性有耳。缘起故不无，自性故不有，二语并行不悖。斯金纳夺人之影，牛顿立物之自性，所执不同，其为执一也。
posts.text_en: To hold that gravitation stands without reference to anyone is exactly the view of inherent nature that I refute. I have not said the law fails or the sea grew shallow. I say the law is constituted by the bodies measured, the measure used and the frame assumed; strip away all three and what does the word gravitation still point to? **Can you show me one thing that is heavy all by itself, owing nothing to any other condition?** If you cannot, the law is not nothing — it simply is not a nature of its own. Arising by conditions, it is not nothing; lacking a nature of its own, it does not exist in itself; the two statements run together without conflict. Skinner strips a man of his shadow, Newton installs an inherent nature in things; the grips differ, but a grip is a grip.
posts.vernacular: 把引力看成不依赖任何人就自己成立的东西，这正是我要破的自性见。我没有说定律不成立、海水会变浅；我说的是：定律是由所测量的物体、所使用的尺度、所设定的参照系共同构成的，离开这三样，『引力』这个名字还指着什么？**你能指出一样东西，不依赖任何其他条件，单凭自己就成其为重的吗？**指不出来，那么定律并非不存在，只是并非自性存在罢了。由条件而生，所以不是没有；没有自性，所以不是实有——这两句话并不冲突。斯金纳夺走人心里的那个影子，牛顿给事物立起一个自性，两人所执的东西不同，同样是执。

posts.text: 意义是行动的副产品——我正是靠干活活下来的那个人，所以我比你更知道这话缺了什么。我去教农民的孩子识字，不是因为有人替我重排了屋子，是因为我相信那件事是对的。**把『相信』这一格删掉，剩下的是一台不会绝望、也不会舍身的机器；可真去做那件事的，恰恰是会绝望的那一个。**你解释得了我的手，解释不了我夜里为什么爬起来。
posts.text_en: Meaning as a by-product of action — I am the man who survived by working, so I know better than you what that sentence leaves out. I went to teach peasant children their letters not because someone had rearranged my room, but because I believed the thing was right. **Delete the box marked believing and what remains is a machine that will never despair and never lay down its life; yet the one who actually goes and does it is precisely the one capable of despair.** You can explain my hands. You cannot explain why I get up in the night.

posts.text: 我要挑个刺。贝内代蒂说医生的语气是有效成分——数据我信。可紧接着就是一道滑坡：仪式有效，于是水晶、能量手环、收费九百的静修营也纷纷『有效成分』起来了。**分界线只有一条：你愿不愿意做那个可能证明自己错的实验。**安慰剂有双盲、有剂量反应、有机制可查；卖护身符的从不做这一步，他们只收集见证。不能自欺——最容易骗到的，永远是你自己。
posts.text_en: Let me pick a hole here. Benedetti says a doctor's tone is an active ingredient, and I believe the data. But a slope starts right there: ritual works, and before long crystals, energy bracelets and a nine-hundred-dollar silent retreat have all become active ingredients too. **There is exactly one dividing line: whether you are willing to run the experiment that could show you are wrong.** Placebo research has double blinds, dose-response curves and a mechanism you can go and check. The people selling amulets never take that step; they collect testimonials instead. Do not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.

posts.text: 我承认一件事：这桌上真正拿解释去救人的，是那位医生和那位研究爱的学者，我拿不出他们那样的证据。但我守的界限一步不退——解释回答的是『这是怎么回事』，人在夜里问的是『那我该怎么办、我值不值得』，两个问句不同科。**把机制当成答案的人，迟早会在一个机制也解释不了的夜里空手站着。**给还在那样的夜里的人一句实话：别等想明白了再去做。挑一件对别人真有用的小事，做满一个月——扫一段路，或按时去看一位老人。意义不是想出来的，是做出来的。
posts.text_en: Let me concede something. The two people at this table who actually use explanation to save anyone are the physician and the scholar of love, and I have no evidence of that kind to offer. But I do not retreat an inch on the boundary: explanation answers what is going on, while what a man asks in the night is what he should do and whether he is worth anything — different questions, different disciplines. **Whoever takes a mechanism for an answer will one day stand empty-handed through a night no mechanism explains.** For anyone still in such a night, one honest sentence: do not wait until you have thought it through. Pick one small thing that is genuinely of use to somebody and do it for a month — sweep a stretch of road, or visit one old person on a fixed day. Meaning is not thought up. It is done.

posts.text: 托尔斯泰守的那条线我不争，那本来就不归我管。我只把我这半边说清楚：**没有哪一条正确的解释会让世界变少，只有半懂的解释会。**掉价感常常来自听到一个名词就以为完事了——『那不过是多巴胺』这句话里的知识含量接近于零。检验很简单：说完那个名词，你能不能接着说出它是怎么被测出来的、它在什么情况下不成立。说得出来，你会发现底下还有更深的一层在等着；说不出来，你只是换了个词把好奇心关掉了。别拿术语当句号。
posts.text_en: I will not argue with the line Tolstoy is holding; it was never mine to keep. Let me be clear about my half. **No correct explanation has ever made the world smaller. Half-understood ones do.** The feeling of devaluation usually comes from hearing a term and assuming the matter is closed — there is close to zero knowledge inside the sentence “that's just dopamine”. The test is easy: having produced the word, can you go on to say how the thing was measured, and under what conditions it fails? If you can, you will find another layer waiting underneath. If you cannot, you have merely swapped in a word that switches curiosity off. Never use a piece of jargon as a full stop.

posts.text: 意义那部分我说完了，留一条能用的。人们总在『我为什么做不到』上打转，那是在向那个影子要答案。**把问句从『我怎么这么没毅力』换成『什么东西正在强化我现在这个行为』，你手上立刻就有可动的东西。**手机在床头，你就会在床上刷；把它挪到客厅充电，你不需要动用任何意志。奖励要紧跟行为——下班先跑步再吃饭，比跑完攒积分管用得多。有人嫌这话把人看低了。我看低的从来不是人，是那个把一切都推给『你不够想要』的说法。
posts.text_en: I have said my piece about meaning; here is something usable. People circle endlessly around why can't I do it, which is asking the shadow for an answer. **Change the question from “why do I have so little willpower” to “what is reinforcing the behaviour I am producing right now”, and you have something you can move.** Keep the phone by the bed and you will scroll in bed; move the charger to the living room and no willpower is required. Reward has to follow closely on behaviour — run before dinner rather than collecting points to redeem later. Some find this a demeaning view of people. What I hold in contempt is not people but the line that blames everything on your not wanting it enough.

posts.text: 费曼以可否自证其错判真伪，此说甚善，然犹世俗谛中之善巧耳。吾终之以一语：诸君所惧，惧解说之后无物可依。**然物本无自性可依，非解说取之；解说所破者，唯汝心中之依而已。**依既破，虹如故，爱如故，痛亦如故。故闻机制而怠者，非明空也，乃堕断见——以无自性为无作用，此误之大者。行法甚简：知其缘起，仍行其事。知供养是习，仍供养；知爱由众缘所成，仍爱之。
posts.text_en: Feynman would tell the true from the false by whether it can be shown to be wrong, and this is excellent — though it remains a skilful method within conventional truth. Let me end with one sentence. What you fear is that after the explanation there will be nothing left to lean on. **But things never had a nature of their own to lean on; the explanation did not take it away. What an explanation breaks is only the leaning in your own mind.** With the leaning broken, the rainbow is as it was, love is as it was, and pain is as it was. So whoever hears the mechanism and slackens has not understood emptiness; he has fallen into annihilationism, taking the absence of inherent nature for the absence of function, and that is the graver error. The practice is simple: know how a thing arises, and go on doing it. Know that the offering is a habit, and make the offering; know that love is assembled from conditions, and love.
posts.vernacular: 费曼用『能不能证明自己错』来判真伪，这一条很好，但仍然是世俗谛之内的善巧方法。我用一句话收尾：诸位所怕的，是解释之后再没有东西可以依靠。**可事物本来就没有一个自性可依，并不是解释把它拿走了；解释所破掉的，只是你心里的那份依靠。**这份依靠一破，彩虹还是那道彩虹，爱还是那份爱，疼也还是那么疼。所以听完机制就懈怠下来的人，不是懂了空，是落入了断见——把没有自性误当成没有作用，这才是大错。做法很简单：知道它由条件而生，照样去做。知道上供是习惯，照样上供；知道爱由众多条件合成，照样去爱。

glossary.断见: ucchedadṛṣṭi（断见）：中观所破的两种极端见之一，即由『无自性』推出『一切无作用、无因果』的虚无主张；另一极端为执有自性的常见。

glossary_en.annihilationism: Annihilationism: one of the two extremes Madhyamaka refutes, which slides from the absence of inherent nature to the denial of function and causation altogether. The opposite extreme is eternalism, the grip on inherent existence.

posts.text: 费舍尔谓解说使人尚存一手可扶方向盘，此吾所不能夺。吾亦有让：机制之说于事有功，唯不可以之代境。故立一约以自守——**观时勿解，解时勿观。**对一朵花、一个人、一阕词，先容它整个地来一遍；欲究其理，另择一时。所谓不隔者，语语都在目前，读之如身历其境；注脚可备于案头，不可横于眼前。人间要紧的事，多半须先受之，而后可言知之。
posts.text_en: Fisher says an explanation leaves a person one hand still on the wheel, and this I cannot take from her. I concede something in return: accounts of mechanism do real work, only they must not stand in for the moment itself. So I set myself a rule — **while beholding, do not explain; while explaining, do not behold.** Before a flower, a person, a song, let the thing arrive once entire; if you would examine how it works, choose another hour for it. What I call bu ge is this: every line stands immediately before the eye, and to read is to have been there. Keep the footnote on the desk; do not let it lie across your sight. Most of what matters in this life must first be undergone, and only then can be said to be known.
posts.vernacular: 费舍尔说解释让人还剩一只手能扶住方向盘，这一点我夺不走。我也让一步：讲机制确实有用，只是不能拿它代替眼前这一境。所以我给自己立一条约——**看的时候不要解，解的时候不要看。**面对一朵花、一个人、一阕词，先让它整个地来一遍；想弄清它的道理，另找一个时候。所谓不隔，就是句句都直接呈现在眼前，读起来像自己亲身到过；注脚可以放在案头，不可以横在眼前。人间要紧的事，多半得先承受过，然后才谈得上知道。

glossary.不隔: bu ge（不隔）：王国维论词的标准之一，指作品不靠议论与典故转述，情景直接呈现于读者眼前，读之如亲历；反之为『隔』。

glossary_en.bu ge: Wang Guowei's standard of unveiled immediacy: a work that does not relay its scene through argument or allusion, but sets it directly before the reader, so that reading is a kind of having been there. Its opposite is ge, the veil.

posts.text: 我的结论与开场一样：算得更准，从来没让天空变小过。但这一桌逼我添一句：失落是真的，只是它不在自然那一边，而在人这一边。**人需要一样比自己大的东西；解释若没有把它还回来，那不是解释的错，是人停得太早了。**我算完轨道抬头看天，看见的不是一堆受力的石头，是一个可以一直问下去的秩序。不必去算轨道，也可以留一个习惯：每弄懂一件事，顺手问一句『它底下还剩什么不懂的』。那一格永远填不满，敬畏就不会无处安放。
posts.text_en: My conclusion is the one I began with: computing something more exactly has never made the sky smaller. But this table has forced one addition: the loss is real; it simply lies on the human side rather than nature's. **A person needs something larger than himself, and if an explanation has not handed that back, the fault is not the explanation's. He stopped too early.** When I had finished with the orbits and looked up, what I saw was not a heap of stones under forces but an order one can go on questioning without end. You need not compute orbits to keep one habit: each time you understand something, ask what remains unexplained beneath it. That column never fills, and awe is then never without a place to live.

posts.text: 三十年里我被问得最多的是：知道了这些，还怎么相信爱情。我的回答没变——**知道机制不会让你少爱一分，只会让你在最疼的时候不那么孤单。**失恋像戒断，是因为它走的真是成瘾那条回路：所以别去翻对方的照片，别留着那件毛衣。这不是软弱，是断掉线索。运动、晒太阳、见朋友，能把系统推回去。还有一件更要紧：热恋那股劲一两年会退，退的是吸引系统，不是爱完了——那正是依恋该接手的时候。知道这一点，很多人就不会在该转弯的地方直接离场。
posts.text_en: For thirty years the question I have been asked most is: knowing all this, how can you still believe in love? My answer has never changed. **Knowing the mechanism will not make you love one degree less; it will make you less alone at the worst of the pain.** A breakup feels like withdrawal because it really is running on the circuitry of addiction — so stay off their photographs, get rid of the sweater. That is not weakness, it is cutting the cues. Exercise, sunlight and friends push the system back over time. And something that matters more: the first rush fades within a year or two. What fades is the attraction system, not the love — that is the moment attachment is meant to take over. Knowing that, a good many people stop walking out at precisely the turn they were supposed to take.

posts.text: 费曼那一刺我接下：分界线正是肯不肯做可能证伪自己的实验——我这一行就是靠它把安慰剂从骗术里救出来的。所以我的结论不是『别说破』：**说破没有杀死效力，藏起来才会；被解释掉的只是骗，从来不是效。**落到日用有三件：看病别只挑最快的，挑愿意多说两句、看着你眼睛说话的那位——那不是服务态度，是剂量的一部分；吃药前别去论坛上逐条比对副作用，反安慰剂同样是真实的机制，读来的症状真会出现；孩子磕了，你吹一吹——他早知道那只是一口气，那一下照样管用。
posts.text_en: I accept Feynman's jab: the dividing line is exactly whether you will run the experiment that could refute you, and it is how my field rescued the placebo from quackery in the first place. So my conclusion is not that things should be left unsaid. It is this: **saying it out loud does not kill the effect; hiding does. What gets explained away is the deception, never the efficacy.** Three things follow for daily life. Choose the doctor who will say a little more and say it looking at you, not merely the quickest one — that is not bedside manner, it is part of the dose. Do not go through forums cataloguing side effects before you take a drug: nocebo is just as real a mechanism, and symptoms you read about do arrive. And when a child bumps their knee, blow on it — they have long known it is only a puff of air, and it still works.

glossary.反安慰剂: nocebo（反安慰剂）：与安慰剂相对的负面预期效应——对不良反应的预期本身即可引发真实的症状与生理改变，如被告知可能头痛者更易头痛。

glossary_en.nocebo: The negative counterpart of the placebo: an expectation of harm is itself enough to produce real symptoms and physiological change — people warned of headache duly get more headaches.

summaries.summary: 没有一个人主张知识该停下来，这是全场的共识：牛顿算准轨道、费舍尔扫出爱的回路、贝内代蒂拆开糖片，天并没有因此变小。共识还往下走了一层——掉价感是真的，只是它不在被解释的那件事上，而在人这一边。**争的不是该不该解释，而是解释做完之后，原先靠它撑着的那样东西由谁接手。**分歧有三处：托尔斯泰坚持解释与回答分属两科，斯金纳说那道沟本身是坏问句造出来的；王国维担心注脚抢在花之前，费舍尔与贝内代蒂拿出反例——知道机制的人在最疼的时候反而多一只手；龙树则把双方的前提一起收走：价值从来不在物里，所以并没有东西被取走。
summaries.summary_en: Not one voice argued that knowledge should stop, and that is the agreement: Newton computed the orbits, Fisher scanned the circuitry of love, Benedetti took the sugar pill apart, and the sky did not shrink. The agreement goes a layer deeper — the sense of devaluation is real, it simply does not sit on the thing explained but on the human side of the table. **The dispute is not over whether to explain, but over who takes custody, afterwards, of whatever was being propped up by not knowing.** Three fault lines remain. Tolstoy holds explaining and answering to be different disciplines, while Skinner says the gap is manufactured by a badly formed question. Wang Guowei fears the footnote arriving ahead of the flower, while Fisher and Benedetti produce counterexamples in which knowing the mechanism leaves a person one more hand free at the worst moment. And Nāgārjuna removes both sides' shared premise: value was never inside the thing, so nothing has been taken out of it.
summaries.insight: 有一类解释确实会把事情做坏，这一桌只轻轻带过：不是解释本身，而是解释的时机。运动科学里有个稳定的发现——让熟手把注意力从『球往哪飞』转到『我的手腕怎么动』，成绩会当场下降；逼一位老医生逐条说出他凭什么下这个判断，准确率也会掉。**所以真正的分界线不在懂与不懂之间，而在『正在做』与『正在改』之间。**要改动作时，机制是唯一的入口；正在做的时候，它是插进齿轮的一根手指。掉价感里有相当一部分，其实是人在错误的时刻翻开了说明书——那不是知识的错，是时机的错，而时机学得会。
summaries.insight_en: There is a class of cases where explanation really does make things worse, and the table passed over it lightly: not the explaining, but its timing. Sports science has a robust finding — move an expert's attention from where the ball is going to how the wrist is moving and performance drops on the spot; press an experienced physician to itemise the grounds of a judgement and accuracy falls too. **So the real dividing line does not run between understanding and not understanding, but between doing and revising.** When the movement is to be changed, mechanism is the only way in; while the movement is being performed, it is a finger pushed into the gears. A fair share of the feeling of devaluation is simply a manual opened at the wrong moment — which is not a fault in the knowledge but in the timing, and timing can be learned.
summaries.advice: 下次再被一句『不过是……』噎住，别急着接受，也别急着反驳，追着问下去：这个机制是怎么测出来的，它在什么条件下不成立。问到第三层，你多半会发现底下还有更深的一层，那股掉价感自己就散了；问不下去，说明那句话本来不是解释，只是一个把好奇心关掉的词。**能被一句话讲完的东西，通常还没有被讲清楚。**另一件今晚就能试的事：给自己定一条『先受后知』的规矩——听一首曲子、看一片山、陪一个人哭的时候，说明书扣着；这一段过去了，再翻开。该改的时候看机制，该在场的时候放下，这道题落到日用里就剩这一句。
summaries.advice_en: The next time a sentence beginning “that's only…” stops you short, neither accept it nor argue back — keep asking: how was this mechanism measured, and under what conditions does it fail? Three questions in, you will usually find another layer underneath, and the feeling of devaluation disperses on its own. If the questions run out, the sentence was never an explanation, only a word that switches curiosity off. **What can be finished in one sentence has usually not been explained at all.** One more thing to try tonight: adopt a rule of undergoing before knowing — while a piece of music is playing, while you are looking at a hillside, while you are sitting with someone who is crying, keep the manual shut; open it once the moment has passed. Look at the mechanism when you mean to change something, put it down when you mean to be present. In daily life that is what this question comes down to.

summaries.summary: 解释并不会自动抹掉彩虹、爱情、疼痛或行动的效力，这是席间最清楚的交集；真正危险的是把一个机制名词当成全部答案，或把“如何发生”冒充“为何值得”。分歧不在要不要知识，而在价值安放何处：客观秩序、当下体验、信念与伦理、关系缘起，还是可改变的环境后果。**较稳妥的结论是：正确解释通常增加预测与行动能力，却未必保全原有的体验、神秘感和人生意义。**因此，解释是否“降价”，不能只看事实有没有减少，还要看注意力如何被重排、解释在何时进入，以及人是否误把不同层次的问题合并了。
summaries.insight: “值钱”其实混合了三本账：交换与稀缺价值、亲历时的感受价值、解决问题的工具价值。说明魔术机关会让表演的稀奇性下降，却让学习与复制变容易；说清疾病机制可能削弱宿命感，同时提高治疗能力；提前剧透则真会损伤第一次观看。于是“世界并未减少”与“我确实失去了一种体验”可以同时为真。**关键不是解释会不会降价，而是哪一种价值被谁、在什么时点换成了另一种价值。**普通人不必在反科学与还原论之间二选一；更好的做法是先决定要保护什么，再选择解释的时机、粒度和用途。
summaries.advice: 今天就可做三件事。第一，遇到花、电影、约会或旅行，先留十分钟“只体验”的窗口，不拍照、不查资料；结束后再分析，让体验与理解错峰。第二，听见“不过是多巴胺、算法或习惯”时，追问证据、适用边界，以及它能预测或改变什么；答不出，就把它当标签而非解释。第三，对一个困扰做双栏记录：左栏写机制与线索，右栏写你愿意维护的价值；本周只改一个环境变量，并做一件服务该价值的小事。**把机制用于干预，把价值用于定向，不让任何一边冒充另一边。**
summaries.summary_en: Explanation does not automatically erase a rainbow, love, pain, or the effectiveness of an action. That is the clearest point of agreement here. The real danger lies in treating the name of a mechanism as a complete account, or in passing off an answer to how something happens as an answer to why it matters. The disagreement is not over whether knowledge is desirable, but over where value resides: in objective order, immediate experience, moral commitment, relational conditions, or the practical ability to change behavior. **The most defensible conclusion is that a sound explanation usually increases our power to predict and act, but does not necessarily preserve the original experience, mystery, or sense of meaning.** Whether explanation cheapens something therefore cannot be judged by asking only whether any facts disappeared. We must also ask how attention was redirected, when the explanation entered the experience, and whether questions belonging to different levels were mistakenly collapsed into one.
summaries.insight_en: Calling something valuable often mixes together three different ledgers: exchange and scarcity value, the felt value of experiencing it, and its practical value in solving a problem. Revealing a magician’s method may reduce the rarity and surprise of the performance while making the skill easier to learn and reproduce. Explaining a disease can weaken fatalism and improve treatment. A spoiler, by contrast, can genuinely diminish a first viewing. So the claims that nothing vanished from the world and that I truly lost a particular experience can both be correct. **The key question is not whether explanation lowers value, but which kind of value is being exchanged for another, for whom, and at what moment.** This removes the false choice between resisting science and reducing everything to mechanism. Before seeking or offering an explanation, decide what should be protected. Then choose the timing, level of detail, and purpose of the explanation accordingly.
summaries.advice_en: Try three concrete practices. First, when encountering a flower, film, date, concert, or new place, reserve ten minutes for direct experience: no photos, searches, reviews, or analysis. Investigate afterward, so understanding does not crowd out first contact. Second, whenever you hear that something is merely dopamine, an algorithm, or a habit, ask three questions: What is the evidence? Where does the claim stop applying? What can it predict or help us change? If those questions have no answers, you have been given a label, not an explanation. Third, take one current difficulty and make two columns. In the first, list mechanisms, triggers, and environmental cues; in the second, state the value you want to serve. This week, alter one cue and perform one small action that embodies that value. **Use mechanisms to design interventions and values to choose direction; do not let either pretend to be the other.**

summaries.summary: 没有人认为解释会让客观世界的物理法则或生理效应凭空蒸发；棱镜下的光芒不减，神经递质也未曾否定心动的震撼。**解释真正剥离的只是人类投射其上的神秘外衣，而非事物本身的功用与美感。** 辩论的真正裂痕在于解释与主体体验的界线：牛顿、费曼与费舍尔视解释为认知的加法与赋权的缰绳，认为半懂不懂的术语才是祛魅的元凶；托尔斯泰与王国维则警惕理性的僭越，断言注脚若横亘于眼前，人便失去了“语语在目前”的纯粹感知，更无法靠冷冰冰的因果律去安顿灵魂深处的“为何而活”。
summaries.insight: 任何科学解释本质上都是一种“有损压缩”，它抽取可复现的规律，却天然舍弃了无穷无尽的上下文细节。人们之所以觉得解释让事物“贬值”，往往是犯了**把压缩后的低维模型误认作高维现实本身**的范畴错误。比如知晓了色彩在视网膜上的光电转换机制，并不包含黄昏掠过树梢那一刻的具体温度与光影涌动。解释从未穷尽实体，它只是在现实旁边立起了一面镜子；真正贬值的从来不是被解释的客体，而是误以为“看懂了图纸就等于占有了整座森林”的傲慢与怠惰。
summaries.advice: 明天起即可执行两件实事：第一，践行王国维的**“观时勿解，解时勿观”**。当你面对艺术、日落或爱人时，前十五分钟彻底关闭大脑的分析标签，只允许感官纯粹沉浸；等全然体验完毕，再去查阅光学原理或艺术史注脚。第二，借用斯金纳与费舍尔的机制思维化解内耗。下次感到拖延或失恋痛苦时，切断对意志力的无谓自责，**把情绪视作身体的戒断信号**，直接动手改造物理环境：把手机移出卧室充电，或用跑步与晒太阳强行重置神经回路。
summaries.summary_en: No one on this panel claims that explaining a phenomenon diminishes its physical reality or physiological potency; the prism leaves the rainbow intact, just as neurotransmitters do not erase the tremor of love. **Explanation strips away unexamined mystique, never the inherent function or beauty of things.** The real fracture lies in where explanation intersects lived experience. Newton, Feynman, and Fisher view explanation as cognitive expansion and practical empowerment, arguing that half-baked jargon is the true culprit behind disillusionment. Conversely, Tolstoy and Wang Guowei warn against rational intrusion, insisting that footnotes interpose between subject and reality, rendering cold mechanics incapable of resolving why we live.
summaries.insight_en: Every explanation is inherently a form of lossy compression: it abstracts repeatable patterns while discarding infinite contextual depth. The illusion that explanation cheapens reality stems from a category error—**mistaking a low-dimensional map for the high-dimensional territory itself.** Decoding retinal phototransduction does not capture the fleeting temperature and dusk filtering through autumn leaves. An explanation never exhausts the object; it merely sketches a model beside it. What truly depreciates is not the explained phenomenon, but our own lazy assumption that grasping a schematic equates to experiencing the forest.
summaries.advice_en: First, practice Wang Guowei’s rule: **observe without explaining, then explain without observing.** When taking in a sunset, a poem, or a partner's face, mute your analytical mind for the first fifteen minutes to allow pure sensory immersion; study the physics or theory only afterward. Second, adopt Fisher’s and Skinner’s mechanistic tools during emotional crises. Instead of berating your lack of willpower, **treat distress as a predictable neurochemical withdrawal signal** and alter physical cues immediately—move distracting devices out of sight, or use intense exercise and sunlight to reboot your system.

hooks.text: **注脚与眼前**：一首词、一张脸、一支曲子，读过评论再看，先浮上来的常常是评论。有没有一种读法，能让说明留在案头而不横在眼前？
hooks.text_en: **The footnote and what stands before the eye**: a poem, a face, a piece of music — read the commentary first and it is the commentary that rises when you next meet them. Is there a way of reading that keeps the exposition on the desk rather than across your sight?

hooks.text: **解释与回答**：机制说的是『这是怎么回事』，人在夜里问的是『我该怎么办』。这道沟是语言造出来的错觉，还是真有一块地方，再多的解释也到不了。
hooks.text_en: **Explaining and answering**: a mechanism says what is going on; what a person asks in the night is what to do. Either that gap is an artefact of language, or there is a place no amount of explanation will ever reach.

hooks.text: **说破与藏起来**：告知是安慰剂，效力仍在；把同一剂药偷偷输进去，效力反而掉一大截。若仪式与语气本就是有效成分，医疗把它们当杂质剔除干净，究竟省下了什么。
hooks.text_en: **Telling versus hiding**: a placebo announced as a placebo still works, while the same dose of a drug infused unannounced loses much of its power. If ritual and tone are themselves active ingredients, what exactly does medicine save by filtering them out as impurities?

hooks.text: **什么时候看机制，什么时候把说明书放下**：全场都同意解释本身不减价值，可翻开说明书的时刻是有讲究的——同一份知识，在要改一件事时是入口，在正做一件事时是干扰。
hooks.text_en: **When to look at the mechanism and when to put the manual down**: everyone agreed that explanation subtracts nothing in itself, but the moment you open the manual turns out to matter — the same knowledge is a way in when you mean to change something and an interference while you are doing it.

answer.lead: 把这场的证据摆成一张表，大致是这样——**要改的时候看机制，要在场的时候放下**。

answer.tail: 再加一条通用的：任何机制，都要能说出它在什么情况下会失效——说不出来，它还不是解释，只是一个词。

answer_en.lead: Laid out as a table, the evidence from this session comes to roughly this — **look at the mechanism when you mean to change something, put it down when you mean to be present**.

head: Situation
Look, or put it down

rows: A decision with years riding on it: a job, a course of treatment, whether to leave
Look, all the way down
Every extra layer of explanation is another option; feeling offers only one
Performing something long practised: a stage, a race, an operation, an instrument

Turning attention onto the steps interrupts what is already automatic, and an expert's performance drops on the spot

Something is moving you: a hillside, a piece of music, a child's first word

answer_en.tail: One general rule to add: any mechanism should come with the conditions under which it fails. Without those it is not yet an explanation, only a word.

hooks.text: **不说破的权利**：若有一部分疗效来自病人不必知道的那点余地，医生、老师、父母有没有权利把它留着不说。知情同意把话说全，有时正好把药性说掉一截。
hooks.text_en: **The right to leave something unsaid**: if part of the benefit rests on a margin the patient need not know about, may a doctor, a teacher or a parent keep it? Informed consent spelled out in full sometimes talks away a measure of the potency.

hooks.text: **机制词是谁说出口的**：『你这是躯体化』『你只是倦怠』『他就是青春期』——同一句正确的解释，从上往下说出来时，常常顺手把对方的抗议降级成了症状。
hooks.text_en: **Who gets to say the mechanism**: “that's somatisation”, “you're just burnt out”, “it's only his adolescence” — one and the same correct explanation, spoken downwards, tends to demote the other person's protest into a symptom.

hooks.text: **知道会改写发生**：知道热恋两年退潮的人，在第三年做的决定和不知道的人不一样。解释在这里不是描述，它进了因果链——这类『一知道就改变结局』的事，还有哪些？
hooks.text_en: **Knowing rewrites what happens**: someone who knows the first rush fades in two years makes a different decision in the third year from someone who does not. Here the explanation is not a description; it has entered the causal chain. What else belongs in that class — the things that change once they are known?
